arxiv-2012-10273.title: Rayleigh-Taylor instability during impact cratering experiments
arxiv-2012-10273.creator: V. Lherm 1, R. Deguen 2, T. Alboussière 1, M. Landeau 3
arxiv-2012-10273.description: A 2020 arXiv research paper by V. Lherm 1, R. Deguen 2, T. Alboussière 1, M. Landeau 3. When a liquid drop strikes a deep pool of a second liquid, an impact crater opens while the liquid of the drop decelerates and spreads on the surface of the crater. If the density of the drop is larger than the surrounding, the interface between the drop liquid layer and its surrounding becomes unstable, producing mushroom-shaped plumes growing radially outward.

arxiv-2203-15267.title: Selective inference for k k -means clustering
arxiv-2203-15267.creator: Yiqun T. Chen, Daniela M. Witten
arxiv-2203-15267.description: Abstract We consider the problem of testing for a difference in means between clusters of observations identified via k-means clustering. In this setting, classical hypothesis tests lead to an inflated Type I error rate. To overcome this problem, we take a selective inference approach.

arxiv-2208-10638.title: Scalable Hybrid Classification-Regression Solution for High-Frequency Nonintrusive Load Monitoring
arxiv-2208-10638.creator: Govind Saraswat, Blake Lundstrom, Murti V Salapaka
arxiv-2208-10638.description: Abstract Residential buildings with the ability to monitor and control their net-load (sum of load and generation) can provide valuable flexibility to power grid operators. We present a novel multiclass nonintrusive load monitoring (NILM) approach that enables effective net-load monitoring capabilities at high-frequency with minimal additional equipment and cost.

arxiv-2301-04338.title: Synthetic data generation method for data-free knowledge distillation in regression neural networks
arxiv-2301-04338.creator: Tianxun Zhou, Keng-Hwee Chiam
arxiv-2301-04338.description: Abstract Knowledge distillation is the technique of compressing a larger neural network, known as the teacher, into a smaller neural network, known as the student, while still trying to maintain the performance of the larger neural network as much as possible. Existing methods of knowledge distillation are mostly applicable for classification tasks.

arxiv-2410-16268.title: SAM2Long: Enhancing SAM 2 for Long Video Segmentation with a Training-Free Memory Tree
arxiv-2410-16268.creator: Shuangrui Ding Rui Qian Xiaoyi Dong Pan Zhang, Yuhang Zang Yuhang Cao Yuwei Guo Dahua Lin Jiaqi Wang
arxiv-2410-16268.description: Abstract The Segment Anything Model 2 (SAM 2) has emerged as a powerful foundation model for object segmentation in both images and videos. The crucial design of SAM 2 for video segmentation is its memory module, which prompts object-aware memories from previous frames for current frame prediction.

arxiv-2505-07683.title: Multimodal Survival Modeling in the Age of Foundation Models
arxiv-2505-07683.creator: Steven Song, Morgan Borjigin-Wang, Irene Madejski, Robert L. Grossman
arxiv-2505-07683.description: Abstract SUMMARY The Cancer Genome Atlas (TCGA) has enabled novel discoveries and served as a large-scale reference through its harmonized genomics, clinical, and image data. Prior studies have trained bespoke cancer survival prediction models from unimodal or multimodal TCGA data.

arxiv-2508-10901.title: Exceptional flat bands in bipartite non-Hermitian quantum crystals
arxiv-2508-10901.creator: Juan Pablo Esparza, Vladimir Juričić
arxiv-2508-10901.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Juan Pablo Esparza, Vladimir Juričić. Flat bands, in which kinetic energy is quenched and quantum states become macroscopically degenerate, host a rich variety of correlated and topological phases, from unconventional superconductors to fractional Chern insulators. In Hermitian lattices, their formation mechanisms are now well understood, but whether such states persist, and acquire new features in non-Hermitian (NH) quantum crystals, relevant to open and driven systems, has remained an open question.

arxiv-2511-10781.title: Peer Code Review in Research Software Development: The Research Software Engineer Perspective Journal: Empirical Software Engineering
arxiv-2511-10781.creator: Md Ariful Islam Malik, Jeffrey C. Carver, Nasir U. Eisty
arxiv-2511-10781.description: Abstract Background : Research software is crucial for enabling research discoveries and supporting data analysis, simulation, and interpretation across domains. However, evolving requirements, complex inputs, and legacy dependencies hinder the software quality and maintainability. While peer code review can improve software quality, its adoption by research software engineers (RSEs) remains unexplored.

pmc-10575212.title: Structural Design and Verification of an Effective-Area Measurement Device Detection System
pmc-10575212.creator: Xiangzi Chen, Ziping Yun, Ting You, Xiangqian Quan
pmc-10575212.description: The effective-area method is a new way to measure aperture area. It defines aperture area by directly using the beam-limiting effect of the aperture in radiometric measurement. Due to the special structure of the measurement device, it is necessary to find a suitable method to design the detection system.

pmc-11300602.title: Lead-free ferroelectrics with giant unipolar strain for high-precision actuators
pmc-11300602.creator: Xuefan Zhou, Jun Zhang, Hang Luo, Yan Zhang, Shiyu Tang, Houbing Huang, Xi Yuan, Miao Song, He Qi, Dou Zhang
pmc-11300602.description: The trade-off between electrostrain and strain hysteresis for piezo/ferroelectric materials largely restrains the development of high precision actuators and remains unresolved over the past few decades. Here, a simple composition of (Bi0.5Na0.5)1-x/100Srx/100TiO3 in the ergodic relaxor state is collaboratively designed through the segregated domain structure with the ferroelectric core, local polarization heterogeneity, and defect engineering.

pmc-11510322.title: Biodegradation of Heterogeneous Industrial Multi-Walled Carbon Nanotubes by Pro-Inflammatory Macrophages
pmc-11510322.creator: Alexander G Masyutin, Ekaterina K Tarasova, Daniil A Samsonov, Galina E Onishchenko, Maria V Erokhina
pmc-11510322.description: Industrial multi-walled carbon nanotubes (ig-MWCNTs) make up the majority of carbon nanomaterials, and human contact with them is the most probable. At the same time, the biodegradation of ig-MWCNTs by phagocytes has not been studied—existing articles consider mainly laboratory-grade/functionalized MWCNTs (l-MWCNTs), in contrast to which ig-MWCNTs are a highly heterogeneous nanomaterial in terms of morphological and physicochemical characteristics.

pmc-12590237.title: Enhancing neuropsychological assessment clinical pathways in Parkinson's disease through the use of technology
pmc-12590237.creator: Elton H. Lobo, Peter Worthy, Deborah Brooks, Kirstine Shrubsole, Dana Pourzinal, Deepa Sriram, Rachel Fels, Ji Hyun Yang, Jacki Liddle, Leander K. Mitchell, Nadeeka N. Dissanayaka
pmc-12590237.description: BackgroundRoutine administration of neuropsychological assessments to evaluate cognitive decline in Parkinson's disease (PD) may not be feasible in current clinical services. This is due to lengthy administration time, lack of specialised neuropsychologists and other limitations in resources. While technology integration could improve efficiency, understanding the existing assessment journey is crucial for successful implementation in clinical services.

pmc-12627292.title: Integration of RASSF1A and TSPYL5 methylation and AFP protein as plasma biomarker for hepatocellular carcinoma diagnosis
pmc-12627292.creator: Haiyan Chen, Yingmin Luo, Linhong Li, Fei Xu, Xiaohuan Lai, Jinlong Li, Xiaomo Li, Wenjie Song, Yang Liu, Dengke Bao, Jiayun Liu, Guanlin Zhou, Shaogui Wan
pmc-12627292.description: BackgroundEarly detection of hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) represents a significant clinical challenge due to the lack of effective biomarkers. Previous studies have revealed abnormal hypermethylation of RASSF1A and TSPYL5 in HCC tissues, prompting further investigation into their utility as potential biomarkers for HCC diagnosis.

pmc-12771223.title: Evaluation of clear aligner treatment for early permanent dentition Angle Class II Division 1 malocclusion in adolescents
pmc-12771223.creator: Miao He, Hai Feng, Yang-Dong Lin, Yong-Juan Guo, Zun-Tai Li
pmc-12771223.description: BackgroundAngle Class II Division 1 malocclusion in adolescents can impair oral health and facial aesthetics, yet evidence on clear aligner therapy is limited. This study aimed to evaluate the clinical efficacy of clear aligner therapy combined with Class II intermaxillary traction for treating Angle Class II Division 1 malocclusion in adolescents during the early permanent dentition stage.

pmc-13059513.title: Oral health and subclinical vascular changes: a cross-sectional ultrasonographic study
pmc-13059513.creator: Şuheda Erdem
pmc-13059513.description: BackgroundPeriodontitis and dental caries are prevalent oral diseases with potential systemic effects. Recent studies highlight a possible link between oral health and cardiovascular diseases via systemic inflammation and endothelial dysfunction. This study investigates the impact of periodontitis and dental caries on cardiovascular health by assessing their associations with carotid intima-media thickness (CIMT) and carotid arterial stiffness (CAS).

pmc-13114298.title: Exploring Cultural Evolution Through Modular Dynamics in Temporal Hashtag Networks
pmc-13114298.creator: Yasuhiro Hashimoto, Hiroki Sato, Takashi Ikegami
pmc-13114298.description: Social media platforms offer unprecedented opportunities to study cultural evolution by analyzing digital traces. This study presents a methodological framework for analyzing the temporal dynamics of cultural modules in hashtag co-occurrence networks. We address the inherent challenges of analyzing dense, skewed, and highly variable cultural networks by introducing a perturbation ensemble clustering approach that distinguishes stable from unstable structural elements.

pmc-13126488.title: Genome-Wide Meta-Analysis for High Myopia Provides Insights into Disease Mechanisms and Reveals a Causal Link to Primary Open-Angle Glaucoma
pmc-13126488.creator: Kazuya Morino, Akira Meguro, Masao Nagasaki, Ikuko N. Motoike, Masato Akiyama, Takahisa Kawaguchi, Shogo Numa, Yuki Mori, Shota Yasukura, Masahiro Akada, Shin-ya Nakao, Takuro Kamei, Ai Nakata, Masaki Takeuchi, Norihiro Yamada, Yuki Mizuki, Takeshi Yoshida, Yukihide Momozawa, Yoichiro Kamatani, Haya
pmc-13126488.description: PurposeTo investigate the genetic architecture of high myopia.DesignA meta-analysis of genome-wide association studies (meta-GWASs).ParticipantsA total of 7867 individuals with high myopic eyes and 21 700 controls were enrolled.MethodsWe performed a meta-GWAS comprising 3910 cases with high myopic eyes and 5718 controls in the discovery stage.

pmc-13214196.title: Heterogeneous grip strength trajectories and clinical determinants in middle-aged and older chinese patients with cardiovascular disease: a group-based trajectory modelling analysis of the CHARLS
pmc-13214196.creator: Shuyan Su, Zexin Chen, Tongchi Xu, Hongchao Wu, Xilun Ma, Ziting Peng, Minping Lin, Xiaoqin Xu, Ruibin Huang, Chaosen Zhong, Haizhu Tan
pmc-13214196.description: BackgroundGrip strength (GS) is a potent biomarker in cardiovascular disease (CVD). However, evidence is scarce regarding the long-term dynamic changes of GS and their multifactorial determinants. This study aimed to identify distinct GS trajectories and their determinants among middle-aged and older Chinese adults with CVD.

pmc-13637124.title: Consensus-based detection of aetiologic copy number variants for syndromic orofacial clefts utilising whole exome sequencing of case parent trios
pmc-13637124.creator: Samuel Kanor Quaynor, Gideon Okyere Mensah, Tamara Busch, Bruce Tsri, Solomon Obiri-Yeboah, Daniel Kwesi Sabbah, Pius Agbenorku, Peter Donkor, Azeez Butali, Lord Jephthah Joojo Gowans
pmc-13637124.description: BackgroundOrofacial clefts (OFCs) are the most common craniofacial congenital anomalies, with complex aetiology involving both genetic and environmental factors. Most genetic studies on the condition have focused on the contribution of single nucleotide variants (SNVs) and small insertions and deletions (indels).
